title: Milwaukee officer sentenced after repeated personal Flock searches
summary: Court reporting by FOX6 Milwaukee and the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel said former Milwaukee police officer Josue Ayala used authorized access to the department's Flock license-plate database repeatedly for personal searches involving an ex-partner and another person. The reports say he later pleaded guilty to attempted misconduct in public office, resigned, and received probation and a fine.

sources.title: Flock search misuse: Former Milwaukee police officer gets probation
key_claims: A criminal complaint said Ayala used authorized database access 179 times for personal reasons.
The report said he searched an ex-partner's plate more than 50 times and another person's plate more than 100 times.
The report said a court commissioner granted two restraining orders against Ayala.

sources.title: Ex-Milwaukee police officer sentenced for misusing department's Flock system
sources.publisher: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel / USA TODAY Network
key_claims: The report said Ayala pleaded guilty after improperly using the department's Flock system to track an ex-partner and that person's partner.
The report said police policy limited Flock use to bona fide law-enforcement purposes.
The report said the court imposed 12 months of probation and a $500 fine, and that Ayala resigned from the department.

statutes_or_policies: Milwaukee Police Department policy limiting Flock searches to bona fide law-enforcement purposes

outcomes: Ayala resigned from the Milwaukee Police Department.
He pleaded guilty to misdemeanor attempted misconduct in public office.
A judge imposed 12 months of probation and a $500 fine on July 15, 2026.
A court commissioner granted two restraining orders, according to the cited reporting.
